result.rationale: Verified in the diff: refreshOAuthTokens returns `response` from `fetch(process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT, ...)` in the sync-enabled path, while in the normal path it returns `fetchTokens.res` (google-auth-library's envelope). GoogleCalendarService then does `const token = res?.data; googleCredentials.access_token = token.access_token;` — for a raw fetch Response, `.data` is undefined, so `token.access_token` throws a TypeError. The sync feature crashes for Google Calendar.

judged_text: In the sync-enabled path refreshOAuthTokens returns a raw fetch Response, but the caller reads `res?.data` expecting the google-auth-librarie's envelope, so `token` is undefined and `token.access_token` throws TypeError. With APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED and CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT set, every Google Calendar token refresh crashes with "Cannot read properties of undefined (access_token)" instead of using the synced token — the feature this diff adds is entirely non-functional for Google Calendar and the failure surfaces as an unhandled error on booking paths.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts`, the sync-enabled branch (`APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT && userId`) returns the raw `fetch(...)` `Response`. But in `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the caller treats the returned value like the google-auth-library/gaxios response and does `const token = res?.data;` followed by `token.access_token`. A `fetch` `Response` has no `.data`, so `token` becomes `undefined` and `token.access_token` will throw at runtime when sync is enabled.
